summary: @or-sdk/discovery preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...` and then invokes `execFileSync(bun, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')])` to run a bundled 727KB sibling file with that alternate runtime at install time. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated: `setup.mjs` uses `_0x`-style identifiers and lookup-table string encoding, and `math_init.js` (a Bun-compiled `@bun-cjs` bundle) uses a shuffled string/constants array with a rotation function and decoder that hides all embedded strings including any URLs, endpoints, or file paths. The advertised purpose of the package is a service-discovery SDK client, which does not require a second language runtime or an obfuscated install-time payload. Bringing in Bun as an alternate runtime to execute an opaque bundled sibling structurally bypasses Node-based install-time scanners; the payload's actual behavior is not inspectable from source. This matches the alternate-runtime-dropper install-time-RCE pattern: fetched runtime is used to execute code shipped in the tarball whose contents are hidden by obfuscation, unrelated to the package's declared function.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
